title: Boundedness and persistence of weakly reversible mass-action systems
coverage:
I read all three LaTeX sections in full: build/sections/01-introduction.tex, 02-affine.tex and 03-dynamics.tex.

Lemma 2.1, checked line by line:
- Step 1: the choice of beta_k against the finitely many type-(k-1) tolerances.
- Step 2: the comparison with (t1,0) that gives p_i >= beta_k on U; the reduction to activity inside the inductive family; and the off-U competitor argument that uses a type-(k+1) label on U∪{j}, including the asymptotic ordering h^{beta_k} = o(h^{beta_{k+1}}).
- Step 3: A_lambda is closed (diagonal argument), B_t is compact and avoids mu = t, so rho_t > 0; the local decay c = o(h^{t+rho_t}) holds.
- Step 4: the finite subcover and endpoint ordering; the existence of q_j; both cut contradictions (mu(p) > q_j and mu(p) < q_{j-1}), with the correct o(·) conversions.

Corollary 2.2 (the uniform bound, by compactness) also checks out.

Section 3:
- The choice of tolerance E and the gap H. The derivation of the sign/gap property (3.4) from |(p-r)·v| < |r·v|/2 is correct, and so is the monomial order (3.5).
- The initial label is forced to have slope zero, and the ceiling F <= M holds. The no-boundary plateau follows from E(0) = 1/2.
- Lemma 3.1 (cut-flux): the return path supplies an upward edge, all downward sources are dominated, and the cut decomposition identity is correct.
- Lemma 3.3 (right derivative of the minimum, and the monotonicity proof with the epsilon trick).
- Proposition 3.4: convexity gives K inside int B_h; the first-exit argument and compact continuation work.
- Corollary 3.5: the Brouwer argument for the positive equilibrium.
- Remark 3.6: the LaSalle step.

I also checked the 2A <-> B computation in the introduction: a-dot + b-dot = b - a^2. I found no step that fails.
main_claim: For any finite weakly reversible mass-action network with positive constant rates and any positive initial point x0, the solution exists for all forward time and stays inside [eps, 1/eps]^d. The proof places x0 inside a compact convex polytope K, contained in the open positive orthant, that every solution starting in K never leaves. K is the maximum set of a finite minimum of affine functions; their slopes approximate the log-exponents with a tolerance that is allowed to be discontinuous, and weak reversibility, applied through a cut-flux estimate, makes F nondecreasing along trajectories.
sibling_notes: The board for family 149 was empty when I checked, so no sibling input was used. I posted my verdict there. Side observation, not a gap: the proof uses the rates only through the bound h^H * sum(kappa) < min(kappa), so the same argument would cover time-dependent rates that stay bounded above and away from zero.
